findings.resolution: packages/core/src/canonical.ts now captures Reflect.defineProperty and Object.create at module init. arrPush installs a fresh own data descriptor at the next index via capturedReflectDefineProperty(arr, key, desc), where desc is a null-prototype object built via capturedObjectCreate(null). This routes through the Array exotic [[DefineOwnProperty]] internal method and never invokes OrdinarySet, so an inherited indexed accessor on Array.prototype cannot execute. arrPop analogously uses Reflect.defineProperty on the own 'length' property. Verified with a reproduction script: an installed Array.prototype[0] accessor whose setter increments a counter drops from 14 invocations to 0 during canonicalEncode([1,2,3]). Four new tests in tests/canonical/monkeypatch.test.mjs assert zero invocations and stable bytes/errors for (a) normal encoding under an inherited Array.prototype[0] getter+setter, (b) normal deep encoding under inherited Array.prototype[0..2] accessors, (c) cycle rejection for Array/plain object/Set under the same hostile accessor, and (d) a throwing hostile setter that must never be invoked.

Ran and recorded all four required gates on the exact corrected candidate revision. npm run compile → exit 0 (tsc -b tsconfig.json, no output errors). npm run boundary → exit 0 (dependency-boundary: OK. 15 workspace packages validated against §14.5). npm run lint → exit 0 (eslint --max-warnings=0 .). npm test → exit 0 (1..171, # tests 171, # pass 171, # fail 0, # skipped 0, # todo 0).

notes_for_reviewer: SPEC_BLOCKERS.md BLOCKER-0001 test-count note was updated from 167 to 171 to reflect the four new hostile-inherited-accessor tests. The blocker itself (task text says '157 pre-existing' while the accepted baseline is 44) is unchanged and remains OPEN; the note preserves the auditable evidence of the actual candidate-state totals.

The fix uses null-prototype descriptors (capturedObjectCreate(null)) rather than object literals so that Reflect.defineProperty's ToPropertyDescriptor cannot be diverted by pollution of Object.prototype (e.g. an inherited 'value' or 'get' property). This is a strict superset of the guarantee the review required.

No changes were made under /constitution. ADR-009 already documents the cycle contract and the shared-reference-encoded-by-value semantics; no ADR edits were required for the two MAJOR findings and none were made.
payload.summary: Closed both MAJOR review findings on iteration 2. Replaced internal array growth in packages/core/src/canonical.ts so all indexed writes go through Reflect.defineProperty (captured at module init) with null-prototype data descriptors, which routes through the array's [[DefineOwnProperty]] internal method and cannot invoke a hostile inherited setter on Array.prototype[i]. Added four focused hostile-inherited-accessor tests to tests/canonical/monkeypatch.test.mjs covering normal encoding, deep encoding across three prototype indices, cycle rejection, and a throwing hostile setter. Executed and recorded exit codes for npm run compile, npm run boundary, npm run lint, and npm test on the exact corrected candidate state.
